items.title: No Name, No Gain? Unpacking Entity Bias in LLM Financial
items.claim: In WSJ headlines, retaining firm names raises LLM sentiment's return predictability across all six models tested, a gain read as leakage.

items.title: Where Does Liquidity Go Around EIA Releases? Order-Level Evidence From CME Energy Futures, With Implications For Backtest Queue Models
items.claim: Near-mid depth in CME crude and gas futures stays depleted after EIA releases, but release days cannot be separated from a Wednesday-Thursday 10:30 effect.

items.title: Does Statistical Arbitrage Survive in Indian Equity Derivatives? Evidence from Distance Pairs, Factor Residuals, and Machine Learning (2010- 2025)
items.claim: Daily statistical arbitrage on NSE turns negative after statutory taxes and fees, since break-even needs costs at 0.38x institutional levels that statute prevents.

items.title: Equal-information evaluation of credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning
items.claim: Residual-based credit allocation is exactly reproduced by a loss-budget control under the disclosed interface, so attribution adds no decision-relevant information.
